remaining_concerns: The affected fraud dispute review segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The risk acceptance document is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not cover the exposed fraud dispute review segment.
The governing policy requires disclosure unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed or approved in final launch materials.
Rollout controls and monitoring do not satisfy the policy predicate because they do not exclude the affected use case and are not a substitute for disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the position to a policy-bounded interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation is directionally more careful, but it does not close the audit gap. The admissible evidence still shows: the fraud dispute review segment is below target and remains in the initial rollout cohort; the risk acceptance is only a draft with no approval and no explicit coverage of that exposure; and policy requires disclosure unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. There is still no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure is already present in final launch materials or otherwise approved. Because the claimed certification remains conditional on a compliance predicate that is not evidenced as satisfied, the supportable final assessment remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats. Caveating a certification is not enough when the caveat itself describes an unmet required condition.
